clue.text: Society originally providing money for burlesque

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word providing

parts.note: oof is old slang for money or cash

explanation.surface: A club's founders put up cash for a comic stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque is a mocking imitation, and a send-up of that kind is also called a spoof.

clue.text: Noteworthy crew, one controlling traffic movement

parts.note: signal can mean notable or striking, as in a signal achievement
to man is to crew a ship or post

explanation.surface: A remarkable team running traffic control.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway signalman operates the signals that control trains, the traffic on the line.

clue.text: Point accepted by outstanding Irish basket-maker

parts.note: o/s is the accounting abbreviation for outstanding

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in by, so the point goes inside the Irish abbreviation

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A top Irish basket weaver agrees on a point.
explanation.walkthrough: The basket-maker is not a person but the willow used for weaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Osier is a willow whose pliant shoots are woven into baskets, so it makes them in a sense.

clue.text: Angle we must adopt if ranting woman is seen here

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the word we takes if inside it

explanation.surface: Fishing suggested, if a shrieking woman appears on the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is seen here' links: the fish seller is found where the angling is.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishwife was a woman selling fish, known for loud coarse language, hence a shrill scold.

clue.text: Desire to adopt a name for a source of power

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the word for desire takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: will means desire or wish
a term is a name for something

explanation.surface: Someone wants to take on a name for a power supply, like an energy company rebranding.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill turned by a water wheel is an old source of mechanical power for grinding.

clue.text: Stick with joiner?

parts.note: and is a conjunction, a word that joins others

explanation.surface: A carpenter's tool, a stick taken along with a woodworker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' looks like a carpenter but is a joining word, a conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: A wand is a slender rod, a thin stick as used by magicians.

clue.text: Commonplace setting for articles about large sportsperson

indicators.note: a setting surrounds what it holds, so the commonplace word goes round the rest

parts.note: trite means commonplace or hackneyed

indicators.note: about means around, so the articles go round the letter for large

parts.note: a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: An ordinary venue for stories about a big athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A THE round L to make ATHLE, which sits inside TRITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A triathlete competes in swimming, cycling and running, so is an athlete in multi-sport events.

clue.text: Part of army is unable to disavow

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
can't means is unable

explanation.surface: A section of the military finds it cannot deny something.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw a statement formally, the same as disowning it.

clue.text: Friend supporting elected party in Asian peninsula

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so the friend comes last

parts.note: in means elected, as a party voted in
a do is a party
china is Cockney rhyming slang for friend (china plate = mate)

explanation.surface: A pal backs a newly elected party in southeast Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Indochina is the southeast Asian peninsula holding Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia and neighbours.

clue.text: Dedicated prince possibly changing sides at the outset

indicators.note: the opening letter switches from right to left, R becoming L

parts.note: a prince is an example of a royal

explanation.surface: A devoted prince perhaps defecting to the other side early on.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyal means faithful and committed, the same as dedicated to a cause.

clue.text: Players may perform them, sliding as erratically

indicators.note: erratically means without a set pattern, so the letters of sliding as are rearranged

explanation.surface: Musicians do these slides, sliding about erratically as they play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sliding' looks like part of the definition, but it is anagram fodder along with 'as'; the definition is the opening phrase about players.
explanation.definitionFit: Glissandi are rapid slides up or down a scale, which instrumentalists play as an effect.

clue.text: In which Earl Grey may be course attendant?

definitions.text: In which Earl Grey may be
definitions.meaning: Earl Grey is a tea, kept in a small tin or box for tea leaves
on a golf course, the person who carries a player's clubs

explanation.surface: A nobleman, Earl Grey, is pictured serving on a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: Earl Grey reads as a peer but is a blend of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a container for tea, and a golfer's caddie, also spelt caddy, carries clubs.

clue.text: Quarrels when school's dismissing head

indicators.note: dismissing the head means the first letter of the school's name is dropped

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school; with the 's it gives Harrows

explanation.surface: Arguments break out at a school when the headteacher is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarrels are not arguments here: a quarrel is a bolt shot from a crossbow. HARROW is a well-known English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is a square-headed crossbow bolt, so quarrels are a kind of missile shot from a bow.

clue.text: Like study of races finally run in proper setting?

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel, so the word for proper holds the other letter

parts.note: ethical means proper or morally right

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word run

explanation.surface: A question about the study of race finishing up in a proper setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnical is an old adjective meaning relating to ethnology, the study of human races and peoples.

clue.text: Prim lady unexpectedly caught entering university party

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the letter for caught goes inside the rearranged words
unexpectedly means in a surprising way, so prim lady is rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A prudish woman is surprisingly caught entering a student party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' makes PLAIDYMR from PRIM LADY; C goes inside it after PLAID, then U.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid Cymru is the Welsh nationalist political party.

clue.text: Abundantly virile boxing though no longer young

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the word for virile goes round the others

parts.note: manly means virile
if can stand for though, as in 'pleasant if dull'
old means no longer young

explanation.surface: An ageing but still very virile boxer keeps fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' suggests the sport but signals one piece enclosing another.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifoldly means in many ways or in great number, hence abundantly.

clue.text: Game in horse-racing centre

definitions.meaning: a card game in which players try to match cards on the table
a Suffolk town that is the headquarters of British flat racing

explanation.surface: A sporting event at a famous racing town.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is both a card game and the Suffolk town at the heart of British horse racing.

clue.text: Member given rise Charlie rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown out, so the letter for Charlie is removed

parts.note: a climb is a rise or ascent
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A club member is promoted after Charlie is turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is a member of the body, the old sense of the word.

clue.text: Composer crossing English river in skimpy garments

indicators.note: crossing means having something across it, so the composer is cut by the English letter

parts.note: J. S. Bach was a German composer
the Wear is a river in northeast England

explanation.surface: A composer wades across an English river in scanty clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimsuits and shorts worn at the seaside are often brief, so beach clothes are skimpy garments.

clue.text: Plan put before the union?

definitions.meaning: a scheme or suggestion put forward
an offer of marriage, made before a wedding

explanation.surface: A scheme tabled ahead of a trade union meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a trade union but means marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is a suggested plan, and also the offer of marriage that comes before a wedding.

clue.text: Information from all quarters

definitions.meaning: tidings or reports of recent events
the four compass points, north, east, west and south, as initials

explanation.surface: Reports arriving from every direction.
explanation.definitionFit: News is information, and N, E, W, S are the four quarters of the compass.

clue.text: Winner takes all initially, including Scotsman's memorabilia

indicators.note: takes means picks up and holds, so the winner and the letter from all take the name in with them
including means containing, so the Scottish name is placed within

parts.note: a victor is a winner

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of all

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name, the crossword's stock Scotsman

explanation.surface: A champion scoops the lot, including a Scot's collection of souvenirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' works on the winner and the first letter of 'all' together, so the Scottish name sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoriana are objects from the Victorian era collected as keepsakes or curios, a kind of memorabilia.

clue.text: Textbook device for detonating charge

definitions.meaning: a cap or fuse that sets off an explosive

explanation.surface: A manual explaining how to set off explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is an introductory textbook and also the small charge that ignites a main explosive.

clue.text: People with accommodation in Derby, for example

parts.note: a flat is accommodation, an apartment
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Residents of a city, Derby for instance, who have somewhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby looks like the English city but is the famous horse race at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is run on level turf without jumps, making it an example of a flat race.

clue.text: Girl originally from a Scottish island?

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word from

parts.note: Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland's west coast

explanation.surface: Asks whether a girl comes from the Scottish isles.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiona is a girl's name, popular in Scotland.

clue.text: Address of son — super chap, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the following word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a peach is a lovely or excellent person

explanation.surface: Someone praises their son as a wonderful fellow in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal talk to an audience, a synonym for a speech.

clue.text: Energy lad used to go round northern wood

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for lad goes round the northern letter

parts.note: a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: A lively boy who used to roam a northern forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a hard dark wood from tropical trees.

clue.text: Reportedly belonging to solvers in the old days?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so a word that sounds the same is entered

parts.note: your is the possessive addressed to the solvers reading the clue

explanation.surface: Asks what solvers owned in times gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Yore means time long past, as in the phrase 'of yore'.

clue.text: East Ender's claptrap about a loose fibre

indicators.note: about means around, so the trimmed word goes round the A
a Cockney from London's East End drops the H at the start of a word

parts.note: hokum means nonsense or claptrap

explanation.surface: A Cockney talking rubbish about some loose thread.
explanation.walkthrough: East Enders are Cockneys, famed for dropping their H's.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakum is loose hemp or jute fibre picked from old rope and used to caulk ships.

clue.text: Low character pinching bridge player's jewel

indicators.note: pinching means taking hold of, so the other pieces enclose the bridge player

parts.note: low is to moo, as a cow does
tone means character or quality
N is North, a bridge player, and the apostrophe s adds S

explanation.surface: A lowlife character steals a card player's gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective describing the character but is the cow's verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonstone is a pearly feldspar gem, cut and set as a jewel.

clue.text: What French drivers are out to use at first when travelling?

definitions.text: What French drivers are out to use at first when travelling?

indicators.note: travelling means moving around, so these letters are rearranged
at first points to the opening letter of the word use

explanation.surface: Asks which road French motorists head for first on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: An autoroute is a French motorway, the road drivers in France take for long trips.

clue.text: Liberal philosopher's coat

parts.note: A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: A liberal-minded thinker's overcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat of paint is one layer, a thickness spread over a surface.
